answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a pearl as the anchor of the cost. A ledge stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a haven...
